steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Combine sauerkraut, tomatoes, sugar, bacon, and black pepper in a 9x13-inch casserole dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly around the edges and caramelized on top, about 2 hours and 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sauerkraut Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This sauerkraut casserole with bacon and tomatoes bakes slowly to allow the ingredients to caramelize thoroughly for a deliciously savory side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Sauerkraut Casserole

recipeInstructions.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Combine sauerkraut, tomatoes, sugar, bacon, and black pepper in a 9x13-inch casserole dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly around the edges and caramelized on top, about 2 hours and 15 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I love this recipe! I've made it several times and I've made these adjustments...First, I crisp the bacon and drain it, so the dish isn't so greasy, then I cut the sugar WAY back to 1/4 of a cup. In a pinch, I used an apple instead of a tomato and it was PERFECT. For a full meal, I also chop up sausage and mix in with the kraut/apple mixture. Just awesome!
I've made this since the nineties. I used brown sugar 1/4 c. While cooking bacon, add about 1/4 up finely chopped onion. Mix all together, bake 325 until bubbly an Carmelized

Tasty with spicy sausages off the grill! I reduced the sugar to 2/3 cup and I think it was just right. Didn't completely mask the sour in the sauerkraut, but gave it a new flavor for sure. I fried the bacon first, but I think I would use a couple of pieces more next time,. We liked it. Easy and something different.

The taste was good. The changes I made were: cut the sugar in half, added smoked sausage because there wasn’t enough meat with just the bacon, used two jars of sauerkraut, and cooked on bake in my Ninja Foodie for 30 minutes. Next time I will add white potatoes because the dish just needed something to offset the richness of it. Overall, it was a good basic recipe.

I had my doubts about this recipe, but the reviews were good, and I did make a few minor adjustments. I cut the sugar to less than half because I used really sweet fresh tomatoes, and reduced the amount of pepper, as well, knowing that if more were needed, it could be added at the table. I scaled this down to 4 servings, and this was done at 2 hours, so watch your time and check often, as you certainly don’t want this to dry out. That mild sweetness and the flavor that the bacon brings to this casserole is simply delicious. Served this with grilled brats which I added toward the end of the casserole cooking. If you’re a sauerkraut lover, you really should give this a try. Thumbs up in this house!
I will likely make it again. When I do, I will reduce the pepper to 1 teaspoon (I used 1/2 tablespoon this time) and reduce the sugar to 1/4 cup or less (I used about 1/2 cup this time).

I made 1/2 recipe as a test. This recipe is yummy. My only change was to cut back on the pepper as my spouse will add his own pepper, anyway. As I ate my test batch, I imagined serving this on a plate topped with grilled bratwurst or slices of roast port loin. I will definitely make this dish again and again.

I am in shock! My 3 year old tried this and asked for more!! He is the world's pickiest eater other than my 6 year old who did not like it--but that means NOTHING! LOL! I loved this--did rinse and drain the sauerkraut, cut back on the pepper and used real bacon bits and petite diced canned tomatoes ( I am lazy!)--this was AWESOME!! I loved it and will make again soon--will cut back on sugar next time just to reduce calories but it was great and I enjoyed it sweet! I am German and this is the real deal!!! :) Thanks for a great recipe!
Very different and excellent. We doubled the recipe and loved it! Recommend cutting down on the pepper (about half would do).Will make believers out of people who don't even like sauerkraut.

This recipe reminded me of a sauerkraut pizza my mom made for my dad's birthday party one year. She just added the very well-drained sauerkraut to a basic cheese pizza, and it was so popular that everyone ate it before my dad even got a piece, so she made another one a few days later. I like the sausage, apples, onion, and brown sugar suggestions or additions. Canned tomatoes will be an excellent substitute for fresh ones, and for chicken rather than pork, chicken sausages can be substituted for the bacon or pork sausage and still deliver a similar flavor profile.
So good - I followed other comments and added chicken sausage and only used 2 tsp sugar. Great recipe!

Turned out great, pretty much as the recipe states. I used 1-14oz. can of diced tomatoes with the juice, drained and squeezed the sauerkraut (not rinsed), I did not brown the bacon beforehand, added 8oz. of apple juice and I used about 2 to 3 tablespoons of honey instead of sugar. That way it fit my Paleo diet.
Made as described. It wasn't very good, but it was edible… barely. Wouldn’t make it again.

This is my favorite go-to recipe for potlucks! Everyone loves it and there are never leftovers to bring home. Just as a matter of taste, i use about 1/2 the sugar. If there are going to be kids, i cut back on the pepper too. I love this recipe!
I loved this recipe, except for one thing. The sugar was way to much. I cut it in half and it was perfect. if not for that it would be five stars.
We had this tonight with our meal and loved it! I only changed the pepper amount. I just sprinkled a little bit and stirred it in, the hubby is sensitive to it!
This was OK. I used kielbasa browned and drained instead of bacon. I enjoyed the sweet/sour flavor.

This casserole was a New Year's Day hit with our family After reading all the pepper cautions, I opted for a 1/2 tsp and this was perfect. I also did 1/4 cup white sugar and 1/4 cup brown sugar which was also perfect. Used diced tomatoes and packaged read bacon bits for convenience. My husband put the leftovers on a hot dog the next day and loved it. Thanks for a great recipe to use on New Year's Day meals.

This was good with a few adjustments. Per other reviews I cut the sugar down to 1/3 cup. Will cut it to 1/4th next time. I also added left over pork roast. Meat was wonderfully tender and flavorful. Did enjoy the casserole...but it was still a little to sweet with the 1/3 cup sugar.
very interesting flavor -- very tasty! Unfortunately, mine turned out a bit greasy, which is the only reason for the 4-star.
